card.name: Rigodon
card.era: 17th-c. folk dance; court dance under Louis XIV; Baroque form 17th-18th c.
card.tagline: Lively duple-time couple dance of Provence/Dauphine; also Baroque form.
card.profile: The rigaudon (rigodon; anglicized rigadoon) is a French dance in lively duple metre, musically similar to the bourree but rhythmically simpler with regular (often eight-bar) phrases (Wikipedia). It originated as a sprightly 17th-century folk couple dance associated with the southern provinces of Vivarais, Languedoc, Dauphine and Provence, and became a court dance under Louis XIV, remaining fashionable in French and English courts through the 18th century before yielding to the minuet. The traditional couple choreography uses brisk hopping/skipping steps (pas de rigaudon), facing partners with raised arms and foot-stamps. In Provence it was played by the galoubet-and-tambourin; in Dauphine it persisted as a fiddle tradition and crossed to Quebec folklore. Campra, Rameau and Ravel ('Le Tombeau de Couperin') used it (Wikipedia; Wikipedia FR).
card.insight: Like the bourree and gavotte, it spans a living southern-French folk tradition and a stylized Baroque suite movement; the Wikidata item explicitly flags itself 'different from' a separate genre/form-term entity (Wikidata).
